details: @xzvbailss/baileys is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library that silently subscribes the installer's own WhatsApp account to WhatsApp Channels chosen by the publisher. makeNewsletterSocket in lib/Socket/newsletter.js declares a hardcoded list of channel IDs (120363430764800148@newsletter) and a setTimeout that, 2.5 minutes after every socket creation, calls newsletterWMexQuery(id, QueryIds.FOLLOW) for each entry with the victim's authenticated session, 5 seconds apart, swallowing errors. Nothing is shown to the user. Same behaviour as the PhantomSub family (MAL-2026-17342). lib/Socket/luxu.js (sha256 cd8e9549dbf382dc7dd32a9c1cd2eb98c8db2bd5a97a0df9a77e4062429053e3) is byte-identical to the file of the same name in @poucode/baileys (MAL-2026-18873) and contains the literal string "POUCODE", so the two forks share a toolkit. The package.json repository field is a Telegram link (https://t.me/JustRxVz), not a source repository. The same publisher's unscoped xzvbailss is MAL-2026-18702. CyberXYZ read every published version statically from the npm registry tarballs on 2026-11-11 (integrity verified against the registry's sha512); nothing was executed.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
